summary: Proceed with two required changes. (1) Source B's per-call set/restore of preferred_blas_library('cublaslt') is forbidden: replace it with a cuBLASLt plan fixed in prepare and held in state, or drop that cell. (2) Drop _bulk_forward's state['bulk_route_hit'] write. The A2 smem budget fits 2 CTAs/SM (99,072 B dynamic each). The Conjecture's mechanism (the qkv row-minus-kernel gap comes from the split-K reduce) is already contradicted by master's own profile, so restate the confirm/refute criteria on kernel time before running.
justification: A. Sources A and B are carried over unchanged from the sibling combo-naive-pooler-m1-rowowner-qkv-m128-cublaslt and are justified by measured rows. Pooler d1: bulk kernel 17.0 us vs swapab 18.7 us (row 17.28 vs 18.93). qkv m=128: nvjet 48x64 single node 16.2 us vs nvjet 96x64 splitK 12.7 us + splitKreduce 3.0 us. The new parts are A2 (qkv_gate m=1, bulk_kernel<16,8192,8,0>, grid 144, 4 stages, 2 CTAs/SM) and A3 (o m=1, bulk_kernel<64,1024,8,0>, grid 128, 6 stages). Geometry checks out. A2: CKK=512, NCHUNK=16, XS=1040, SLOT=16384+8*1040=24704 (24704%128==0), and R*CKK*2=16384. KSW=8 per consumer warp, kbi<=7, so each chunk is 8 kblocks x 16 rows x 128 B = 16 KB. _bulk_repack's [c][kb][row][64] layout makes each chunk contiguous at (c*NCHUNK+j)*16384 B for any R, so no repack change is needed. The epilogue N=gridDim.x*R=2304 is correct. scratch [4][16][8] fp32 = 2 KB, which aliases the ring safely. A3: CKK=128, NCHUNK=8, XS=272, SLOT=18560 (18560%128==0), KSW=2, MT=4, dyn smem 256+6*18560=111,616 B, 1 CTA/SM, grid 128 = 8192/64. SMEM FIT for the (160,2) variant: dynamic smem = 256 + 4*24704 = 99,072 B per CTA. Adding sm_90's 1 KB per-block reservation gives 2 x 100,096 = 200,192 B, under the 233,472 B (228 KB) per SM. It fits with about 33 KB to spare. Five stages would not fit (2 x (123,776+1,024) = 249,600 B), so 4 is the deepest ring that allows 2/SM. Registers are not binding (65536/320 = 204/thread; acc is 4 floats at MT=1, NN=1). Note that __launch_bounds__(160,2) only caps registers; the smem carveout decides whether the second CTA is co-resident. WEAKEST LINK: the Conjecture's premise. Master's own data contradicts it. Pooler m=1 on master also runs a split-K ticket reduce (SWAPAB16_CFG pooler SPLIT_K 2), yet its row-minus-kernel gap is 0.2 us. o m=1 runs SPLIT_K 1 with no reduce, yet its gap is 2.1 us. Source A's pooler win came entirely from kernel time (18.7 to 17.0 us); the gap went 0.23 to 0.28 us, essentially unchanged. So the gap does not track the reduce. At small row times it is more likely a fixed ramp-up or profile-vs-graph-row artifact, and 'gap shrinks below ~1 us' cannot discriminate. On kernel time alone, A2 must beat 9.6 us for 37.7 MB (3.93 TB/s). The row-owner kernel's best observed effective rate was ~3.95 TB/s (67.1 MB / 17.0 us), which projects to ~9.5 us, about flat. It also gets half the ring depth (4 stages, 64 KB/CTA in flight) and an uneven 144-on-132 placement: 12 SMs host two CTAs and stream 512 KB vs 256 KB. The expected 12.7 to 10.5-11 us is therefore optimistic. A 'master kept' outcome from A2's gate is the most likely result and is a valid refutation, which the run CAN read off the PATH CHOSEN line and the profile. A3 is a sound control-like cell: 8 chunks cannot amortise a 6-stage fill, so the gate should keep master. Expected directions are consistent with TASK floors (qkv d1 7.9 us, o d1 3.5 us, pooler d1 14.0 us, qkv m128 8.4 us). The total upside is about +0.8% from the sibling's cells plus at most ~0.3-0.7% from A2, below the ±1.5% headline CI. Attribution must come from the per-cell gate prints and the profile rows, not the headline.
confounders: bf16-restack-m16-swapab-router-swapab-m32: defines the incumbent at qkv_gate/o/pooler m=1 (swapab16: qkv SPLIT_K 4, o SPLIT_K 1, pooler SPLIT_K 2). It is the comparison point for A/A2/A3, not a confounder. However, the qkv incumbent's 3.1 us gap and o's 2.1 us gap come from this path's rows, and the pooler (SPLIT_K 2, 0.2 us gap) shows that the gap is not the reduce.

sglang-gemm-dispatch-parity: defines the qkv_gate m=128 incumbent (_bf16_gemm_dispatch_impl -> nvjet 96x64 splitK + splitKreduce) that Source B replaces. It is the control for B, and the cell gate compares against it directly.

restack-three-cell-wins-router-unpooler-cluster-m8-nn-m128 / pooler-nn-layout-widen-m256: no shared shapes (unpooler slice m<=8, router m<=8, NN layout m>=65 on pooler/unpooler only, not qkv). They are relevant only through prepare budget and import-time build time: ouns + router_cluster + bulk builds are all inside the 10-minute run limit, so log each build's seconds.
router/bf16 Triton landings: different layers and shapes, no interaction beyond the shared cold-L2 timing method.
interference: No companion. Every new cell is behind its own in-prepare A/B gate, which prints both medians (graph replay, 256 MB flush, 41 interleaved reps) and the chosen path. With the required torch.profiler kernel-name assertion, each scored row is attributable without another run: a routed cell shows bulk_kernel or the Lt kernel in the profile with its own µs, and a non-routed cell is byte-identical to master. The sibling combo-naive-pooler-m1-rowowner-qkv-m128-cublaslt is already the natural 'minus A2/A3' control if both are submitted. Even if it is not, A2's and A3's contributions are read from their PATH CHOSEN lines plus the qkv_gate/o decode_1 rows vs master's 12.67/5.97 us. A third scored run would buy nothing the gate prints do not already give.
rules_flags: REQUIRED (policy, Source B): the save/set/restore of torch.backends.cuda.preferred_blas_library('cublaslt') inside kernel_fn is per-call mutation of a process-global flag. Standing policy forbids it even though the judge's static check once passed it. Replace it with a prepare-time cuBLASLt plan held in state. Port the load_inline Lt extension from muse_bf16_proj/hypotheses/done/neutral/bf16-cublaslt-algo-pick-in-prepare-m128-m256.patch (candidates() + run() with a prepare-allocated workspace and the algo row in state). For qkv_gate m=128, choose the heuristic candidate with split-K 1 (no reduction node), the one matching the toggle's nvjet_sm90 48x64 tile. Either filter the candidates on CUBLASLT_ALGO_CONFIG_SPLITK_NUM == 1, or query the heuristic with the same workspace cap torch's Lt path uses; a 32 MiB cap ranks split-K algos first. Gate it like every other cell (cand/master <= 0.98, rel L2 vs fp64 within 1.10x of the incumbent's). kernel_fn then calls run() with the state's algo row and workspace, with no global state touched. If the extension build fails or no split-K-1 candidate passes, keep master for that cell, which drops it. A lighter alternative: torch.addmm(zero_bias_bf16[n] from prepare, x, W.t()) takes torch's cublasLt bias-epilogue path without any global preference, but its heuristic pick may differ, so it must pass the same gate and the profile assertion.

REQUIRED: delete the line state['bulk_route_hit'] = (layer, m) in _bulk_forward (source b3e80b45 line ~1052). It is a per-call state write. If prepare needs route proof, use the profiler kernel-name assertion the hypothesis already specifies.

bulk_launch's `static bool attr_set` + cudaFuncSetAttribute(MaxDynamicSharedMemorySize) is a lazy one-time init. Make sure every instantiation (including the new <16,8192,8,0,S=4> and <64,1024,8,0,S=6>) is first launched in the prepare canary, never first inside the judge's graph capture.

For the (160,2) A2 instantiation, also set cudaFuncAttributePreferredSharedMemoryCarveout = cudaSharedmemCarveoutMaxShared (100) next to the max-dyn-smem attribute. Then assert cudaOccupancyMaxActiveBlocksPerMultiprocessor(bulk_kernel<16,8192,8,0,4>, 160, 99072) == 2 in prepare and print it. If it reports 1, the 144-CTA grid runs as two waves: disable A2 for that cell and keep master rather than letting the gate decide on a two-wave kernel.

No other rules issues: weight repacks are lossless permutations verified bit-exact; the output torch.empty is shape-sized; routing branches only on cfg layer/m/n, x shape/stride/alignment and state flags; no host syncs in kernel_fn; precision is bf16 inputs with fp32 mma accumulate and one bf16 store.
open_questions: Restate the Conjecture's confirm/refute criteria before running; the hypothesis md can be edited, the code is unaffected. Confirmed: A2's gate routes (cand <= 0.98x) AND the profile's bulk_kernel<16,...> time is < 9.6 us AND the qkv decode_1 row < 12.3 us. Refuted: the gate keeps master, or the kernel time is >= 9.6 us. Drop 'row-minus-kernel gap < 1 us' as the discriminator, because master's pooler (SPLIT_K 2, gap 0.2 us) and o (SPLIT_K 1, gap 2.1 us) already show the gap does not track the reduce. Also drop 'A3 wins means the effect is TMA issue, not reduce removal', since o has no reduce to remove and a win there is just a faster stream.
With 144 CTAs on 132 SMs at 2/SM, 12 SMs carry double bytes. Print the gate's candidate median next to a projected 37.7 MB / 3.95 TB/s = 9.5 us, so a loss can be split into ring-depth vs imbalance.
The A2 template adds a stage-count parameter. Make sure bulk_launch's smem formula, the kernel's S, and bulk_inst_info's printed 'dyn smem' all use the same template S, not the BULK_STAGES #define.
Prepare/import budget: log each load_inline build's wall time (ouns, router_cluster, bulk, Lt) and each gate's seconds. The whole run must finish inside 10 minutes including timing.
